newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday due to a fall on the domestic A share markets and the weekend factor, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 16.0 percent from 19.52 percent on Thursday.
Combined turnover of the six-contract market fell to 9.52 million lots from 13.2 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Prices of A shares fell on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets on Friday mainly due to a technical correction.
"The fall on the A market was the key factor today," one trader said.

In addition, the weekend, when the exchanges close, sees early-maturing contracts lose two days of effective usage, causing their rates to drop sharply. The rate for three-day contracts plunged to 5.28 percent from 19.5 percent.
Traders said the rates would shortly recover and go up early next week due to an increased number of new A share issues and an expected recovery of the A share markets next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up on a technical rebound after falls in the past few weeks.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 116.25 yuan from 115.96 yuan. Volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.04 million lots from 1.09 million.

Traders said the recent bull run on the A share markets and an increased number of A share issues had dampened sentiment on the spot market. They said the contracts would lack momentum to rise further next week.
But the contracts have annual yields of around 10 percent on average, against 7.47 percent for one-year bank deposits. This will prevent them from falling sharply, traders said.
